answer: Bind each agent identity to one DNS domain it controls through DNSSEC and a TLS certificate, like a cedar staking a single deep root. Registration and renewal fees make every extra identity cost real money, and aged domains are scarce, so a sybil farmer faces a rising bill instead of free copies. A signed, timestamped heartbeat, the domain pulse, proves the agent still controls it, while the horizon of renewal deadlines forces continuous upkeep. Limit: bulk cheap domains still allow small sybil sets, so pair this with rate limits.
